newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WAUGH HAMMERS TEST WARNING WITH CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH HAMMERS TEST WARNING WITH CENTURY.

text.p: Steve Waugh handed West Indies a
warning with a timely Sheffield Shield century for New South
Wales on Friday, just seven days before the first test in
Brisbane.
Waugh's Australian captain and opener Mark Taylor also
showed useful form before the five-test series gets under way by
scoring 53 in New South Wales' 274 for seven at the close of the
first day of the four-day match against Queensland.
Waugh was out for 106 late in the final session, yorked by
paceman Mike Kapsowicz, the best of Queensland's bowlers, who
finished with three for 88 from 20 overs.
Taylor survived two early chances before he was caught by
Kasprowicz from the bowling of left-arm spinner Paul Jackson.
In Melbourne, former test batsman Dean Jones gave a
reminder of his ability with an unbeaten 121, his 51st
first-class century, as Victoria reached 270 for five against
South Australia.
Jones rescued his side after the loss two early wickets
with only 10 runs on the board, and received valuable support
from Ian Harvey, who scored 70.
South Australia's attack was weakened when left-arm paceman
Mark Harrity was hampered by a leg injury.
In Perth, Tasmania reached 122 for one at the end of a
rain-affected first day against Western Australia.
Opener Jamie Cox made 62 before he was trapped leg before
wicket by captain Tom Moody's medium pace. Dene Hills was 48 not
out at the close.
